svg.text: H. Temperature sensitivity of the registered diffusion correlations
Release fraction at 300 h at temperature against test temperature, one curve per registered coefficient variant; log scale
C16-T2-published: published heating-test correlation as printed (Collin 2016 Table 2, rows C16-T2 and C16-BUF), chosen by the strato-data selection function
kernel-radius-scaled: kernel coefficient scaled by (kernel radius 174.85 µm / reference radius 250 µm)^2 = 0.489 (decision 41; sensitivity case, not a published coefficient)

S20-fitted-SiC: SiC replaced by the AGR-1 fitted row S20-01 (Schappel 2020, fitted to the 1600 and 1800 °C heating tests); labelled alternative, never the default; it disagrees with Collin's correction factors by 4 to 220 times (decision 40)
S20-T3-fitted-SiC: SiC replaced by the AGR-1 single-particle fit row S20-10 (S20-T3); labelled alternative, not the default
A3-21-SiC: SiC replaced by register row A3-21 (Russian Fed.; printed range 1200-2300 °C)
A3-14-SiC: SiC replaced by register row A3-14 (Japan; printed range 1600-1900 °C)
A3-15-SiC: SiC replaced by register row A3-15 (Japan; printed range 1600-1850 °C)

The default correlation prints no validity range, so the sweep covers the registered heating-test temperatures 1600 to 1800 °C; of 135 sweep points, 0 lie outside a printed range of a row they use. Variants other

than the published default are labelled alternatives, never defaults (decisions 40 and 41); the class of each coefficient is in the sensitivity file. The AGR-1 fitted silicon-carbide rows of Schappel (2020,

S20-fitted-SiC) are fitted to AGR-1 heating-test data and disagree with the correction factors of Collin (2016) by 4 to 220 times (decision 40). Model: STRATO BTCS five-layer spherical finite difference, package

version 1.0.1, commit e483c9b8869214fea88352ee9debebfa66f904ba; registered AGR1-B-M16 geometry; published heating-test diffusion coefficients chosen by the strato-data selection function (register sets C16-T2 and
C16-BUF), evaluated at the test temperature; kernel-only start; constant temperature; decay and generation are not in the solver. This is a numerical comparison, not an experimental validation.
